files.Title: TDMaker.Editor.LevelDryRun
files.Summary: Headless content check: bakes a level and runs the simulation without rendering. The undefended run calls every wave as early as possible with no towers (shows total threat); the fortified run builds and upgrades towers on every slot with unlimited gold, buys every tower ability, spawns the level's heroes (moving them to the front enemy and spending skill points), and casts ready spells at the leading enemy (checks that every build, branch, rally, ability, move and cast is accepted and that the level can be completed). The budget pass plays with the level's real starting gold: it starts the first wave, lets later waves arrive on their timers and spends gold greedily (builds slots in list order, cycling the buildable towers, then the cheapest upgrade, branch or ability rank), with the same hero and spell assistance (checks that a sensible defense wins).

files.Title: TDMaker.Editor.SampleContentGenerator
files.Summary: Generates the "Basic" sample: projectiles, enemies, soldiers, four tower families, five waves on two multi-lane paths, status effects (slow, poison, stun, rally buff, shield ward), purchasable abilities on final branches (including a chain-lightning ability, a knockback ability, a channelled beam, a path-transfer rift and a trap-laying barracks), a support enemy with a shield cast and a permanent pulse-only healing aura, an armored enemy that reflects damage, one hero (with life steal and a trap skill), two spells (reinforcement and area strike), a level asset and a ready-to-play scene. All content is original and uses hand-authored vector art with procedural fallbacks; the scene uses the uGUI with a theme asset, a fitted camera, a painted ground and the IMGUI HUD as an F1 debug overlay. Re-running updates the existing assets in place. The same run also generates the Crossroads and Winding Pass levels (which reuse the Basic towers, enemies and hero) and the Demo scene (title, level select, pause and result flow over all three levels), plus the English and Korean sample string tables (Samples/Text) that every sample scene's Game Settings use, and the dynamic Korean fallback font asset of the sample HUD themes (Samples/Fonts).

files.Title: TDMaker.Editor.SampleScreenshot
files.Summary: Plays the sample scene with a scripted run (build on every slot, upgrade, call waves early) and renders the main camera, HUD included, to a PNG (for store-page drafts). Works from the menu and from batch mode (-batchmode -executeMethod TDMaker.Editor.SampleScreenshot.Capture, without -quit: the editor exits by itself). Needs a graphics device, so it does nothing under -nographics. Options: -tdmSeconds N (game seconds, default 50), -tdmWidth/-tdmHeight (default 1920x1080), -tdmOut folder (default .work/screenshots), -tdmScene path (default the Basic sample scene), -tdmName file (PNG name without extension), -tdmGold N (starting gold, default 4000), -tdmUpgradeEvery S (game seconds between scripted upgrades, default 1.5), -tdmCallEvery S (game seconds between early wave calls, default 8) -tdmSlots N (build on the first N pads only, default all), -tdmNoHud (map only, for key art) and -tdmShot mode: beam (default: waits for a channelled beam or chain lightning), barracks (waits for soldiers blocking several enemies), hero (sends the hero to the fight and casts every ready spell just before the shot) or worldmap (alias levelselect: the demo scene's world map with preview progress in a throw-away slot; use with the demo scene) or title (the title and its language buttons), or slots (the demo scene's save slot page over the same throw-away store) or shop (the world map's star-upgrade shop over the same throw-away slot, with a few ranks bought and one rank's tooltip shown). -tdmMenu build opens the build menu on the first pad left empty by -tdmSlots instead of a tower panel; -tdmHidePause keeps the frozen capture from showing the paused state. -tdmDemoLevel N starts battle N of the demo scene through its flow (instead of driving the scene's own runner); -tdmPanel opens a tower panel in every shot mode (normally only the beam mode shows one). -tdmLang code (for example ko) shows the HUD and menus in that language of the scene's text tables (not saved to PlayerPrefs). Demo-scene modes levelinfo (the world map with a level's info panel open) and controls (the How to Play page); -tdmPauseMenu opens the pause menu in battle shots. Script errors logged during the run are counted and reported, so the batch run doubles as a play-mode smoke test.

files.Title: TDMaker.Editor.UnitMath
files.Summary: Unit Workshop numbers that follow the simulation's integer damage rules exactly (single-target hits without status effects or incoming multipliers): a hit rolls ceil(lerp(min, max, u)), projectile hits deal at least 1, the target keeps floor(rolled × (1 − reduction)) (soldiers: round(rolled − floor(rolled × reduction))), and the reduction is the matching defense minus pierce (explosion and electric use half the physical armor), clamped to [0, 1]. Ratio checks use the bands of the balance notes (new content starting points, not rules).

The ratios stay inside the bands of the balance notes: bounty density ×0.5–1.8 of the baseline, defenses in the low (0–0.2), medium (0.2–0.5) and strong (0.5–0.7) bands, hero experience steps ×1.1–1.6 after a first jump of ×2.5–3.5. They are a starting point; tune the result against your own towers.

A searchable list (create from presets, duplicate, rename, delete, see who uses an asset), an animation preview (art set frames, Faces Left check, health bar, pivot, projectile flight), tabbed flat forms (basics, attacks, mechanic cards, effects and tags, look with bulk frame registration, hero growth, audio, engagement places), computed values that follow the simulation's damage rules, and a sandbox that plays the unit against chosen towers. files.Summary: Graph view of a tower's upgrade tree (level 1 → 2 → 3 → branches). Each node shows its cost, cumulative investment and sell refund; clicking a node edits it inline. files.Summary: Base class for ScriptableObjects that provide a custom to an ability, skill or behavior action (). The created action is shared by every entity using the asset, so keep it immutable and store per-entity state in a custom component.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.BeamData

files.Summary: Per-level camera framing for maps larger than the screen: how much of the map one screen shows, where the view starts and an optional intro pan along the first path. Read by TDCameraController; presentation only (no simulation effect).

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.CameraFramingMode

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.CameraStartFocus
files.Summary: Where the camera looks when the level starts.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.ChainAttackData
files.Summary: A chained attack that jumps from target to nearby target without revisiting, baked into . Use it as an ability action ().

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.ClickAreaSettings
files.Summary: Per-content override of the HUD's click target: an axis-aligned world rectangle around the entity position (the interior is clickable, the border is not) and a priority added to the kind's default (heroes 1, everything else 0). When several targets contain the click, the higher priority wins, then the lower world reference point.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.CombatModifierData
files.Summary: Reversible combat changes carried by a status effect or passive, baked into .

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.CompanionData
files.Summary: Owner-bound companion slots on a hero or tower, baked into a (template custom data). Each slot keeps one child alive: a ground escort (an ordinary soldier that blocks and follows the owner's move or rally orders) or a flying follower (keeps near the owner, never blocks, attacks from where it is). A fallen child is replaced after , counted from its death. Child damage earns the owner experience.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.CompositeAbilityAction
files.Summary: Runs several custom actions as one channel payload; succeeds when any of them succeeds.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.DamageData
files.Summary: Serializable damage packet baked into , with an optional payload.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.DeathSuccessionData
files.Summary: Extra rules for the enemies released by (successors), baked with : a shared chain budget (successors of successors), a rise time and the bounty rule. A lineage never pays its bounty twice and leaks only once.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.EnemyAsset
files.Summary: A path-following hostile unit.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.EngagementGuestData
files.Summary: Where this soldier or hero stands when it blocks an enemy (the engagement guest): its share of the horizontal gap, added to the enemy's share. See .

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.EngagementHostData
files.Summary: Where blockers stand around this enemy (the engagement host). Blockers stand on the side the enemy is walking toward, host X + guest X world units away horizontally, shifted by the summed Y values. The second and third blocker take rows at −/+ on Y (pulled back by half of it on X); later blockers repeat the three places. Independent of melee range. Typical X: half the enemy's drawn body width plus a small gap.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.EntityAssetBase
files.Summary: Base class for ScriptableObjects that bake into a core .

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.FacingMode
files.Summary: How a view mirrors itself to face its movement direction.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.HealingData
files.Summary: Health restoration, baked into . Not affected by damage multipliers or defenses.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.HeroAsset
files.Summary: A player-controlled hero: base stats, growth rows (experience → level → skill points), skills and respawn. Add it to ; the runner spawns it at the level's hero spawn point.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.HeroLevelData
files.Summary: One hero growth row. Values scale the hero's base stats to produce the absolute row the simulation uses.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.ImpactPayloadData
files.Summary: Extra work after a resolved hit, baked into : a secondary blast, a residual region (which may be pulse-only) and/or a path displacement (negative distance = knockback toward the entry).

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.LaneBuilder
files.Summary: Generates parallel sub-lanes by offsetting a center line along mitred normals.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.LevelAsset
files.Summary: A complete level: geometry, waves, economy and the towers the player may build. Call to produce a and .

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.LevelAuthoring
files.Summary: Combines a (waves, economy, towers) with scene geometry from and components. Empty lists are filled from children in hierarchy order.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.LevelMusicData
files.Summary: Music of one level, played by TDMaker.Unity.View.MusicPlayer: a battle loop, an optional intense loop for late or boss waves, and victory / defeat stingers that stop or duck the loop. Empty clips fall back to the music player's defaults, so every field is optional.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.LevelRulesData
files.Summary: Level-wide economy and flow rules, baked into .

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.LifeStealData
files.Summary: Heals the attacker (or the hero credited with the hit) by a share of the health this packet actually removed, baked into .

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.MechanicTargetData
files.Summary: Extra recipient eligibility for mechanic actions, baked into . Defaults accept everyone.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.MechanicVisual
files.Summary: View-side look of a keyed mechanic (chain, multi-target attack, region pulse, trap, mines, beam, transfer, reflection, life steal, body raising), collected while baking.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.MechanicVisualKind
files.Summary: What a belongs to, where the view treats it specially.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.MeleeData
files.Summary: Serializable melee attack; disabled data bakes to no melee slot.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.MineFieldData
files.Summary: Automatic mine laying, baked into a with a payload. Each activation picks one lane node of a level path inside the distance band around the producer (seeded, deterministic), reserves it, throws the mine (flight, landing, then the arm delay) and leaves a trap that bursts under the first eligible unit. The lifetime counts from the throw. Use it as an ability action (); it fails, without a fallback spot, when no node fits.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.MultiTargetAttackData
files.Summary: One activation that hits several distinct targets at once, baked into . Towers pick targets by their current priority; other actors pick the nearest first.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.PathAuthoring
files.Summary: Scene authoring for an enemy path. Points are in local space; sub-lanes are generated from the center line using and . In curve mode () the user edits a few and is regenerated as a smooth curve sampled every units (see ).

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.PathData
files.Summary: A path authored as a center line; parallel sub-lanes are generated from it.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.PathDestinationData
files.Summary: An exact point on a level path, baked into . Validated against the level when used: an invalid destination (path, lane or node outside the path's entry..exit range) moves nothing.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.PathGeometry
files.Summary: Authoring geometry helpers: smooth curves (centripetal Catmull-Rom) sampled into simulation nodes, and nearest-point queries on path center lines. Used by curve mode and the editor's Map Editor.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.PathTransferData
files.Summary: Moves nearby path-following enemies to an exact path destination (a rift, a recall), baked into . Use it as an ability action (); hits can transfer through .

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.PeriodicDamageData
files.Summary: Damage over time with integer rolls, baked into .

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.PeriodicHealingData
files.Summary: Periodic healing carried by a status effect, baked into .

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.PointRuleData
files.Summary: Shared placement validation for spells and hero movement, baked into .

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.PresentationHooks
files.Summary: Optional per-template presentation hooks: VFX prefabs (pooled) and audio cues for the standard moments of a unit's life. Every field may be left empty.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.PrimitiveShape
files.Summary: Generated placeholder shapes used when no prefab is assigned.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.ProjectileAsset
files.Summary: Projectile travel and presentation data shared by ranged attacks.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.RaiseRemainsData
files.Summary: Raises new units from the bodies the fallen leave behind, baked into a . Each activation reserves the closest eligible bodies (ties by body order), casts for , then consumes each body and creates there (an enemy continues the body's path; a soldier fights for the player). A moved, stunned or dead caster releases its reservations. Bodies decay after the runner's Remains Lifetime. Use it as an ability action ().

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.RangeShape
files.Summary: The single source of the range ellipse used by every view, gizmo and editor preview. It matches the simulation (Simulation.RangeDistanceSquared): a point is inside when dx²/r² + dy²/(k·r)² ≤ 1 (boundary included), with k = range Y scale. The horizontal semi-axis is r and the vertical semi-axis is k·r, so k < 1 flattens the ellipse vertically (an oblique top-down look).

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.RangedAttackData
files.Summary: Serializable ranged attack channel.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.RecoveryData
files.Summary: Health recovery, baked into .

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.ReflectionData
files.Summary: Returns a share of the health actually lost by this unit to its attacker as a single hit, baked into . Shield absorption and overkill do not count; reflected hits never reflect again or steal life.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.ReviveData
files.Summary: Same-unit return on the spot, baked into a (template custom data): a killed unit lies down, then gets of its health back, rises and walks on with the same identity. Its bounty is paid once, on the first death. Pending returns hold victory.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.ShieldData
files.Summary: A damage-absorbing shield carried by a status effect, baked into .

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.SoldierAsset
files.Summary: A friendly unit produced by a barracks tower to block enemies.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.SpawnEntryData

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.SpellKind

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.StatusEffectAsset

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.StrikeData

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Authoring.SummonData

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Hud.ClickPicking
files.Summary: Battlefield click-target rules used by (input grammar, spec 14 §1): every clickable thing has an axis-aligned world rectangle placed relative to its reference point; a click hits it only strictly inside (the border is excluded). Among the hits the higher selection priority wins, then the lower world reference point (smaller y). Equal priority and equal y keep the first candidate found.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Hud.DamageNumbers
files.Summary: Pooled floating damage and heal numbers (TextMesh Pro, outlined) on a screen-space canvas. Numbers are merged per target for a short window so rapid hits do not flood the screen; digits come from a cached string table and fading uses the canvas renderer alpha, so steady-state updates do not allocate. Toggle with .

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Hud.GameHud
files.Summary: Production HUD for PC (mouse + keyboard), built in uGUI from code and styled by a : top bar (gold, lives, wave, pause, speed), wave-call indicators at path entrances (countdown ring, early bonus), radial build menu, tower panel (upgrades, branches, abilities, target priority, rally, sell), hero portraits, spell bar with cooldowns and hotkeys, unit info, pause and victory/defeat screens, tooltips and world feedback (range ellipses, slot highlight, placement ghost, rally/move markers, spell aim). Interaction follows the input grammar of spec 14 (docs/specs/14-input-grammar.md): one selection or aiming state at a time; a battlefield left click acts at the release point; while a hero, rally point or spell is being aimed every battlefield click is a point attempt (valid: act and return to browsing; invalid: feedback and keep aiming); build, upgrade, branch, ability, sell and wave call are single clicks; right click cancels everything (and does nothing without a selection); Esc cancels a selection, otherwise opens/closes the pause menu. Failed or cancelled aims send no command and every result shown is read back from the simulation. Keys: Esc cancel/pause, Space/P pause, 1-9 spells, H hero, N next wave, F1 debug overlay. Text is TextMesh Pro; every string comes from (keys in ), and the HUD relabels itself when the language or a table changes.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.Hud.HudButton

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.View.AudioCuePlayer
files.Summary: Plays s through a small pool of AudioSources and routes global game events (waves, building, selling, victory ...) and mechanic events (chains, traps, mines, beams, heals, shields, reflection, knockback, companions, returning units, body raising) to cues. Per-template cues (attack, hit, death, projectiles, spells) are routed by ; the HUD plays the interface cues (click, build menu, rally, wave call). Every slot is optional. Volumes come from (Master × SFX or UI) and each channel may route to an AudioMixerGroup. Each cue respects its , at most Max Voices Per Cue copies play at once and the pool never grows past Voices (the oldest voice is reused), so dense fights do not stack sounds or allocate.

files.Title: TDMaker.Unity.View.SimulationRunner
files.Summary: Owns a and advances it with the core from Update (catch-up limit = catch-up ticks × speed per frame). Events produced during a frame are dispatched in emission order through and then cleared, so the event buffer (Event Capacity) must hold every tick a frame catches up (at most catch-up ticks × speed). Commands queued after the game ended are rejected by the core with on the next frame (the clock no longer steps, so the runner flushes them).
